hero.title: Cybersecurity Engineering Student
hero.bio: I'm drawn to active defense: monitoring, incident detection, and response, the work of a SOC (Security Operations Center). I build security monitoring systems, log centralization, real-time detection, alerting, that I audit and harden myself, and I study the security challenges specific to AI-integrated platforms. Final-year engineering student in computer science and networks at EMSI (2024 – 2027), seeking a final-year (PFE) internship starting January 2027.

about.heading: Security engineering, from first principles.
about.paragraph1: I'm an engineering student specializing in cybersecurity, oriented toward monitoring and defense (SOC): log surveillance, incident detection, and response. I'm also interested in secure software development and, more recently, the security challenges specific to AI-integrated systems. I like understanding how things break well enough to help build ones that don't.
about.paragraph2: That interest shows up in my projects: SecureWatch, a security monitoring stack with log centralization, real-time incident detection, and alerting, which I self-audited and hardened, an LLM auditing platform, and a self-monitoring virtualized network built around proper segmentation. I put the same mindset to work during my cybersecurity internship at YAZAKI Morocco.

securewatch.title: SecureWatch
securewatch.description: A self-hosted security monitoring stack: log centralization, real-time incident detection, and infrastructure metrics across a microservices architecture, built and then deliberately attacked to find its own weaknesses.
securewatch.problem: Small teams need real visibility into logs, alerts, and incidents without standing up a full commercial SIEM.
securewatch.solution: A Dockerized stack combining an ELK pipeline, an authenticated API gateway, and Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager monitoring, with role-based access and a live attack-geography view.
securewatch.status: Self-audited and hardened: found and fixed 10 vulnerabilities, including a forged-JWT authentication bypass, stored XSS in the log viewer, and unauthenticated exposure of Elasticsearch and Prometheus.

Geographic attack map plotting live threat sources

sentinelllm.title: SentinelLLM
sentinelllm.description: An LLM security auditing platform. It runs structured red-team tests (prompt injection, jailbreaks, unsafe code generation, PII leakage, and more) against any connected model, maps findings to the OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS, and generates exportable PDF audit reports.
sentinelllm.problem: Teams wiring LLMs into products have no structured, repeatable way to test for prompt-injection risk or benchmark findings against recognized security frameworks.
sentinelllm.solution: A FastAPI backend that queues test batches through Celery, scores each response with rule-based and OWASP/MITRE ATLAS-mapped judging, and exports PDF reports, paired with a React/TypeScript dashboard for managing models, launching audits, and reviewing results.
sentinelllm.status: In active development, with model integrations for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Mistral, and local models via Ollama, and CI running on every push.

Launching an audit: target model, test categories, and scoring mode
An audit running live, tracked test by test
Completed audit results, with verdict, OWASP and MITRE ATLAS mapping, and confidence per test, including a caught prompt-injection failure

networkSupervision.title: Network Inventory & Monitoring Platform
networkSupervision.description: A self-monitoring virtual network built as EMSI cybersecurity coursework: three Ubuntu Server hosts running real services, discovered and inventoried by a custom scanner, then continuously watched through a live Zabbix dashboard.
networkSupervision.problem: Network administrators need an accurate, current picture of what's running on their network, and an immediate alert when something goes down, not a discovery made after the fact.
networkSupervision.solution: A VirtualBox lab of three Ubuntu Server hosts (SSH, Apache, vsftpd, SNMP) paired with a Bash scanner that combines Nmap and SNMP to detect hosts and services, plus a Zabbix 6.4 and PostgreSQL deployment that auto-discovers new devices in under a minute and raises, then auto-resolves, alerts as machines go down or recover.
networkSupervision.status: Built with a teammate over a semester: covers host and service discovery, real-time CPU, RAM, network, and disk monitoring, automatic device discovery, and automatic alerting end to end.
gallery: The VirtualBox lab: three Ubuntu Server VMs (Serveur-Linux, PC-Client-1, PC-Client-2) with verified connectivity between all three hosts
All three hosts registered and monitored in Zabbix, tagged by OS and role
Live per-host metrics collected in Zabbix: CPU, memory, disk, filesystem, and network interface data
The Zabbix dashboard: host availability, problems by severity, and live events, including a real captured host restart and a briefly unavailable agent

faceRecognition.title: Real-Time Face Recognition System
faceRecognition.description: A Django application for real-time facial detection and identification via webcam, built partly as an exploration of the privacy trade-offs in biometric systems.
faceRecognition.problem: Understanding facial recognition well enough to reason about its privacy implications means building one, not just reading about it.
faceRecognition.solution: OpenCV and the face_recognition library handle detection and matching in real time, with a registration flow for new faces and image-upload identification.
faceRecognition.status: Functional end-to-end demo, from live webcam feed to identification.

secureEcommerce.title: Secure E-commerce Platform
secureEcommerce.description: A Laravel storefront with a product catalog, shopping cart, and role-based accounts, built with secure defaults rather than bolted-on protection.
secureEcommerce.problem: E-commerce apps are a common target for authentication and session-handling mistakes.
secureEcommerce.solution: Laravel's built-in protections (hashed credentials, CSRF tokens, validated input) applied consistently across cart, checkout, and account flows.
